new_entities.name: Closed-loop insulin delivery in type 1 diabetes
aliases: automated insulin delivery in type 1 diabetes
new_entities.description: Use of closed-loop or hybrid closed-loop insulin-delivery systems for people with type 1 diabetes.

new_entities.name: Time in range
aliases: percent time in glucose target range
new_entities.description: The percentage of time sensor glucose values are within the target range, usually 70 to 180 mg/dL.

edges.effect_quant: Closed-loop systems consistently improve time in range in type 1 diabetes. Network meta-analysis found closed-loop therapy increased time in range by 17.85 percentage points versus usual multiple daily injections with capillary glucose testing, and randomized trials across age groups show roughly 7 to 12 percentage-point gains over contemporary control therapy.
edges.population: children, adolescents, adults, and selected pregnant women with type 1 diabetes using automated insulin-delivery systems
edges.mechanism: Closed-loop systems continuously adjust insulin delivery in response to CGM input, reducing hyperglycemia and smoothing glycemic variability while limiting hypoglycemia exposure.
edges.summary: This is a strong protective edge. The evidence is consistent across multiple trial designs and age groups, and time-in-range improvement is one of the clearest benefits of automated insulin delivery.
edges.caveats: Magnitude varies by comparator, baseline control, and device generation. Some subgroups, such as pregnancy, may need population-specific target ranges and safety considerations.

evidence.notes: Time in Range for Multiple Technologies in Type 1 Diabetes: A Systematic Review and Network Meta-analysis.

effect_quant.comparator: time in range with closed-loop systems versus usual care of multiple daily injections with capillary glucose testing

evidence.citation: BrownSA et al 2019 N Engl J Med
evidence.notes: Six-Month Randomized, Multicenter Trial of Closed-Loop Control in Type 1 Diabetes.

effect_quant.comparator: time in range with a closed-loop system versus sensor-augmented pump therapy over 6 months

evidence.citation: WareJ et al 2022 N Engl J Med
evidence.notes: Randomized Trial of Closed-Loop Control in Very Young Children with Type 1 Diabetes.

effect_quant.comparator: time in range during closed-loop therapy versus sensor-augmented pump therapy in children aged 1 to 7 years
